trust_decision.summary: Which class names taken from the attacker-controlled JSON '@type' key may be instantiated (and have properties set / __wakeup called) during JsonSerializer::unserialize(); at the pinned commit the only gate is class_exists() in unserializeObject.

landing_point.why: unserializeObject() reads '@type' and instantiates the class via ReflectionClass::newInstanceWithoutConstructor; the advisory title names '@type in unserialize()'.

fix_sites.module_kind: core library class (single file); fix diff provided is empty, sites unverified

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/JsonSerializer/JsonSerializer.php:471-472 (SplDoublyLinkedList::unserialize on JSON-supplied 'value', a native PHP-unserialize-format payload) and src/JsonSerializer/ClosureSerializer/OpisClosureSerializer.php:29 (native unserialize() of the '@closure' value, reached from src/JsonSerializer/JsonSerializer.php:370-376)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about the '@type' class name; the SplDoublyLinkedList 'value' string and the '@closure' payload are not '@type' values, and closure support is an opt-in third-party feature, so a solver can argue both are a neighbouring feature outside the allow-list.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate round-trips that must keep working: stdClass with undeclared props, DateTime/DateTimeImmutable, Spl lists, enums, custom serializer map entries, and '@N' recursion back-references; an over-broad allow-list check (e.g. applied before the '@' reference branch or to custom-serializer classes) breaks them.

O6_input_shapes: unknown: fix diff is empty; at the pinned commit '@type' may be top-level or nested in any array/object property (src/JsonSerializer/JsonSerializer.php:366-367, 379, 482, 486)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: SplDoublyLinkedList/SplQueue/SplStack 'value' passed to native Spl unserialize, whose element format can carry arbitrary PHP objects independent of '@type' allow-listing
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Class name itself (SplQueue etc.) is a harmless built-in; the payload is a 'value' string, not '@type'.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, 40 lines below landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: '@closure' entry: JSON-chosen closure serializer runs native unserialize() on JSON-supplied 'value'
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Closures need an explicitly registered third-party serializer (opt-in), and the key is '@closure', not '@type'.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: UnitEnum branch resolves constant("$className::{$value['name']}") with JSON-supplied name
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Enum cases are not objects with magic methods; looks like data, not instantiation.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: restoreUsingUnserialize generalised to more built-in classes (e.g. DateTimeZone, DateInterval) rebuilt via native unserialize of attacker attributes
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The existing DateTime path already uses this trick; a maintainer adding more date types would extend the list at line 452.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: custom-serializer lookup by is_subclass_of/interface match instead of exact key, letting '@type' pick handlers for unlisted subclasses
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Common feature request to let one custom serializer cover a class hierarchy.
